avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin C (>2000mg daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May increase urinary crystallization risk and nephrotoxicity; ganciclovir already poses renal toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin C intake to <1000mg daily; ensure adequate hydration

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (as supplement/OTC)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive nephrotoxicity and reduced renal clearance of ganciclovir, increasing drug accumulation
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; use acetaminophen for pain management instead

avoid_supplements.name: Nephrotoxic herbs (Aristolochia, Creatine loading)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Synergistic renal dysfunction with ganciclovir's known nephrotoxicity
avoid_supplements.action: Strictly avoid; monitor baseline and periodic renal function tests

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ganciclovir may alter gut flora; probiotics support intestinal health during antiviral therapy
caution_supplements.action: Use standard doses; may provide benefit but no direct interaction

caution_supplements.name: Electrolyte supplements (sodium, potassium)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Monitor electrolytes as ganciclovir can cause abnormalities; supplementation should be guided by lab values
caution_supplements.action: Only use with physician guidance based on serum electrolyte monitoring

avoid_foods.name: Excessive dietary potassium (high-K fruits, leafy greens in large amounts)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Ganciclovir can cause hyperkalemia; high potassium intake may compound electrolyte imbalances
avoid_foods.action: Maintain moderate, consistent potassium intake; avoid large servings of bananas, spinach, potatoes

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May affect fluid retention and electrolyte balance during antiviral therapy; maintain consistent intake
caution_foods.action: Maintain moderate sodium intake; avoid sudden dietary changes

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: While ganciclovir is not CYP3A4-dependent, grapefruit may affect general drug metabolism and fluid balance
caution_foods.action: No strict contraindication but avoid excessive consumption; maintain hydration with water

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function (serum creatinine, BUN, eGFR) and electrolytes (especially potassium) regularly during ganciclovir therapy due to inherent nephrotoxicity risk. Ensure adequate hydration (1.5-2L daily unless contraindicated) and avoid all nephrotoxic agents and supplements.
